draft.briefing: Hey, you're in Punalur! The 400-foot suspension bridge here was designed to shake when walked on, to stop animals crossing from the forest into town.
draft.hungryLine: Punalur sticks to local Kerala cooking, so ask what's fresh today at the nearest eatery.

moodReplies.show-me-around: Punalur Suspension Bridge is a 2 min walk. St. Mary's Cathedral Church is about 14 min on foot.
moodReplies.somewhere-to-chill: Go fishing on the Kallada River, or sit by the water near the old bridge.
moodReplies.surprise-me: The Kollam-Shencottah railway through Punalur was the first railway line in the old Travancore state.

legends.title: Where Jatayu fell
legends.body: Legend says Jatayu, the giant bird of the Ramayana, fell here after failing to stop Ravana from taking Sita away. It's a huge rock in Chadayamangalam, great for trekking.

legends.title: A very old Sastha
legends.body: Achencoil's Sastha temple is famous for a Sastha installed several centuries before the Christian Era. It's 80 km from Punalur and an important pilgrim centre.

tips.title: See the Sabarimala temples.
tips.body: Achankovil, Aryankavu and Kulathuppuzha, all linked to Sabarimala, are near Punalur.

tips.title: Ride the old line.
tips.body: The Kollam-Shencottah line, now broad gauge, still runs through Punalur station.

story.title: A bridge that shakes
story.body: The Travancore Government built the 400 ft suspension bridge across the Kallada. It's the only one of its kind in south India.

story.title: Travancore's first railway
story.body: The British commissioned the Kollam-Sengottai section as part of the Kollam-Chennai metre-gauge route. It was the first railway line in Travancore.

story.title: Paper mills and rubber
story.body: Workers from the Punalur Paper Mills, the railway and rubber estates, along with farmers, made up the early community of St. Mary's, the town's first church.

story.title: Broad gauge and the Kallada
story.body: The old metre-gauge line has been fully converted to broad gauge. Punalur is the headquarters of its taluk and revenue division, on the Kallada at the foot of the Western Ghats.
